title: Receiving a DuckDB result without rounding
text: DuckDB can hand result Arrow stream, zuarrow converts directly. default conversion refuses, error names column, row ways receive exactly. lossy = "character" key arrives exact text, arrow_array() turns text back int64. package registers exact class int64, zuint, makes default conversion exact, argument .
code: fetch_arrow <- function(con, sql) {   res <- DBI::dbSendQuery(con, sql, arrow = TRUE)   on.exit(DBI::dbClearResult(res))   reader <- duckdb::duckdb_fetch_record_batch(res)   stream <- nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream(reader)   arrow_to_r(stream, lossy = "character") } res <- DBI::dbSendQuery(con, sql, arrow = TRUE) stream <- nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream(   duckdb::duckdb_fetch_record_batch(res) ) arrow_to_r(stream) #> Error in `arrow_to_r()`: #> ! Column `key` (Arrow format `l`) cannot be converted to R exactly: row 1 holds 9007199254740993. Load zuint to read it exactly, or use `lossy = "character"` for its exact text, or `lossy = "allow"` to accept the loss. DBI::dbClearResult(res) out <- fetch_arrow(con, sql) out$key #> [1] "9007199254740993" "1"                #> attr(,"arrow_type") #> [1] "l" arrow_array(out$key) #> <zuarrow_array int64[2]>
